drills.name: D1 — un / uun length-and-contour discrimination
drills.spec: Beat at 60 bpm, one token per beat. Tutor plays a randomized 20-item string of un / uun. Learner taps LEFT for un, RIGHT for uun, then echoes. Pairs: 'un.' -> learner marks yes; 'uun.' -> no; 'un?' (rising) -> 'huh?'; 'uun.' -> no. Then reverse: English cue ('say yes' / 'say no'), learner produces, native audio checks. Direct payoff of the weeks 1-2 mora-timing block.
drills.target: 18/20 correct discrimination and no leaked English 'uh-huh' on production.

drills.name: D2 — backchannel over a monologue
drills.spec: Tutor speaks 60 seconds of Japanese the learner cannot parse. Learner must place a token in every pause: aa / hee / soo / naruhodo / sokka / honto? / majide? Rule: never the same token twice running. [pause] -> 'aa.'; [pause] -> 'hee.'; [pause] -> 'naruhodo.'; [pause] -> 'honto?'
drills.target: 12 or more placements in 60s, all in-pause, no back-to-back repeats.

drills.name: D3 — greeting call-and-response sprint
drills.spec: Rapid situational cue -> chunk. 'It's 8am, neighbor' -> 'ohayoo.'; 'you bump someone' -> 'ano, chotto sumimasen.'; 'leaving for the night' -> 'jaa ne, oyasumi.'; 'food arrives' -> 'itadakimasu.'; 'plate is empty' -> 'gochisoosama.'; 'colleague heads home' -> 'otsukaresama.'; 'first meeting' -> 'yoroshiku.'; 'friend has an exam' -> 'ganbatte.'
drills.target: Under 0.8s latency on all 12 cues, two clean passes.

drills.name: D4 — extraction toolkit under pressure
drills.spec: Tutor drops one unknown Japanese word into a stream every 15s. Learner fires the right tool: unknown word heard -> "'___' tte nani?"; couldn't catch it -> 'sumimasen, moo ichido onegai.'; too fast -> 'ano, yukkuri onegai.'; wants an English-to-Japanese lookup -> 'nihongo de nan te yuu no?'
drills.target: 4/4 tools fired correctly and unprompted inside a 2-minute stream.

drills.name: D5 — copula paradigm against a beat
drills.spec: One form per beat, cycling: soo da / soo desu / soo ja nai / soo datta / soo deshita / soo ja nakatta. Then randomized: 'plain, negative' -> 'soo ja nai.'; 'polite, past' -> 'soo deshita.'; 'plain, past negative' -> 'soo ja nakatta.'; 'polite, present' -> 'soo desu.' de wa nai is played to the learner but never requested.
drills.target: Full 6-form cycle twice with no dropped beat; 10/10 on randomized cue.

drills.name: D6 — kosoado grid, column then row
drills.spec: Read DOWN the columns first (kore/kono/koko/koo/konna, then the so-, a-, do- columns), then ACROSS the rows (kore/sore/are/dore). Then cue by coordinate: 'row 3, A-column' -> 'asoko' plus the spoken flag that the pattern predicts *ako; 'row 1, DO-column' -> 'dore', plus the observation that the whole DO- column is accent [1].
drills.target: All 20 cells produced from coordinates in under 45s; learner states the asoko irregularity unprompted.

drills.name: D7 — adnominal plus noun substitution
drills.spec: Fixed frame 'kono ___ da yo' with kono/sono/ano/dono rotating and the day's nouns filling the slot. 'this car' -> 'kono kuruma da yo.'; 'that box by you' -> 'sono hako da yo.'; 'which chair?' -> 'dono isu?'; 'that person over there' -> 'ano hito da yo.' Runs daily from day 7 using the newest 12 nouns.
drills.target: 24 substitutions in 90s with correct accent on the noun.

drills.name: D8 — final-particle prosody
drills.spec: One segmental string, six tails, meaning carried entirely by the ending: 'soo da.' (flat statement) / 'soo da ne.' (seeking agreement) / 'soo da yo.' (informing) / 'soo da yo ne.' (assert plus check) / 'soo da na...' (musing) / 'soo?' (rising, doubting). Tutor plays one, learner names the stance in English; then reverse, English stance -> Japanese tail.
drills.target: 6/6 in both directions; learner never attaches ka to a plain form.

drills.name: D9 — 'X ga' accent discrimination (heiban vs odaka)
drills.spec: Pairs where the bare noun is acoustically identical and only ga reveals the accent: 'hito ga' [0] vs 'inu ga' [2]; 'sara ga' [0] vs 'hako ga' [1]; 'kaze ga' [0] vs 'ame ga' [1]; 'kabe ga' [0] vs 'kagi ga' [2]; 'hoshi ga' [0] vs 'tsuki ga' [2]. Learner marks DROP-ON-GA or NO-DROP.
drills.target: 16/20. This drill is the reason every noun is stored in the ga frame.

drills.name: D10 — N no N chains
drills.spec: Build two- then three-link chains. 'my brother's car' -> 'ani no kuruma.'; 'my friend's house's window' -> 'tomodachi no ie no mado.'; 'the top of the desk' -> 'tsukue no ue.'; 'my family's cat' -> 'uchi no kazoku no neko.'; then the question form: 'where's this from?' -> 'kore, doko no?'
drills.target: Ten chains, at least four of them three-link, with no dropped no.

drills.name: D11 — location-noun wheel
drills.spec: Fixed head noun, rotating relational noun: 'tsukue no ue / shita / naka / soto / mae / ushiro / tonari / yoko / chikaku / soba'. Then cued from English: 'under the chair' -> 'isu no shita.'; 'inside the box' -> 'hako no naka.'; 'right beside the chair' -> 'isu no soba.' (soba is produced only inside this frame, never bare.)
drills.target: All ten relational nouns produced from English cue in under 60s.

drills.name: D12 — live mining
drills.spec: Tutor talks for three minutes about the room. Each time the learner hears an unknown noun they interrupt with "'___' tte nani?", write the romaji themselves, and re-use the item within 30 seconds inside 'kore, ___?' or '___, doko?'
drills.target: Three items mined, transcribed in correct Hepburn (doubled long vowels, doubled geminates, n' before a vowel), and re-used in a sentence.

drills.name: D13 — full-sentence copula beat
drills.spec: English cue -> full Japanese sentence, one per beat. 'Is this a cat?' -> 'kore, neko?'; 'This isn't a desk.' -> 'kore, tsukue ja nai.'; 'It's that car over there.' -> 'ano kuruma da yo.'; 'It was over there.' -> 'asoko datta.'; 'Where was the key again?' -> 'kagi, doko datta kke.'; 'It's my brother's car.' -> 'ani no kuruma da yo.'

drills.name: D14 — block A cumulative shadow
drills.spec: A 4-minute scripted conversation built from block-A inventory only, with no topic wa anywhere. Learner shadows at 0.8x, then 1.0x, then produces the second speaker's lines from English prompts alone. Closes on the two capstone frames: 'shikata ga nai.' and 'kane ga nai.'
drills.target: Shadowing at 1.0x with no more than three dropped morae; both capstone frames produced cold.
